pages: After what seemed like an eternity at sea, Odysseus finally awoke upon the shores of an unfamiliar island...
Wandering the beach, he found the scattered remains of his ship and began collecting what little was left of it, not knowing why he felt compelled to do so.
Something within him told him that these broken pieces held the memories of a journey he could no longer remember...
As Odysseus wandered the shores, a woman approached him from the island, seeing the exhaustion that had taken hold of the once great warrior.
Calypso, the nymph of Ogygia, offered him a strange lotus flower, telling him that it would ease his suffering and help him recover from the trials he had endured.
Unbeknownst to Odysseus, the lotus would not only heal his body, but also quitely suppress the memories of the journey that had brought him here...
As Odysseus ate the lotus, he fell into a deep sleep, and within his dreams fragments of his forgotten journey began to return...
He saw himself upon a battered ship with his soldiers, drifting upon a windless sea with little food left and their vessel barely holding together from the storms they had survived.
With nowhere else to go and hunger taking hold of his men, they sailed onward until they finally spotted land upon the horizon...
Driven by hunger, Odysseus and his men rushed onto the island in search of food, where they soon found a great herd of sheep wandering the land.
Following the herd, the starving soldiers came upon a vast cave filled with food, wine and livestock, believing that at last they had found what they needed to survive.
But the cave was not empty... it belonged to a creature far greater than any man, and they had just wandered into the home of the Cyclops.
Before Odysseus could lead his men away, the Cyclops returned to his cave and found the strangers who had entered his home.
Polyphemus, the one eyed son of Poseidon, seized the soldiers and dragged them into the darkness as Odysseus rushed forward to save his men.
But before they could escape, the Cyclops rolled a great boulder across the entrance, trapping them within his cave...
Days passed within the darkness of the cave, as Polyphemus returned each day to feast upon Odysseus' men and drink from his great barrels of wine.
With every passing day their numbers dwindled, while those who remained could only watch and wait for their inevitable fate.
But Odysseus refused to accept that this was where their journey would end... and began to devise a plan to escape.
